scope: Release-based parry, independent aim/jump inputs and selected remaining damage rules. Ultimate parity and human balance remain incomplete.

changes.title: Release-based parry
changes.behavior: Shield raise and hold use ordinary blocking. Release after at least three held simulation frames opens a five-tick parry window (ages 0–4). A successful parry prevents percent damage, shield damage and shield stun, and consumes the window. Reholding cancels the release attempt; a new shield entry resets it. Shield-stun input buffering remains limited.
changes.limit: Attacker gets 11 additional hitlag ticks, an explicit custom advantage. Complete Ultimate parry hitstop, projectile exceptions, shield-drop timing and repeated-hit interactions are not certified.

changes.title: Independent aim and jump
changes.behavior: UP is a new 0x0800 bit in the uint16 input mask; validators accept 0x0000–0x0fff. Up selects tilts, smashes, aerials, specials, up throws, dodge direction and vertical DI/SDI. It does not trigger a jump. Jump buttons do not add upward aim. Known old default Up keys migrate, while unrelated custom action keys remain intact.
changes.limit: No tap-jump toggle or sustained analog walking was added. Existing bit-based walk/run and movement prediction remain approximate.

changes.title: Directional short-hop attacks
changes.behavior: Simultaneous jump+attack captures the attack direction at entry to jump squat and launches the corresponding neutral, forward, back, up or down aerial. Ordinary short-hop aerials deal 85% damage; aerial specials do not inherit that reduction. Double jump, landing and incoming hits clear short-hop context.
changes.limit: This does not implement a full Ultimate action buffer or every shortcut/controller option.

changes.title: Damage precision and match-size scaling
changes.behavior: Damage retains fractions instead of flooring each contact. A match that starts with two participants applies 1.2× percent damage; three/four-participant matches retain group scaling even after eliminations. Shield damage and base knockback are not multiplied by the one-on-one factor. Throws, pummels, counters and ordinary/floor hits follow the match-size damage rule; hit events carry scaled damage, with zero for a confirmed parry.
changes.limit: Existing stale-move, rage, knockback, crouch-cancel and counter-rounding formulas remain project approximations. This pass does not certify their numeric Ultimate parity.

sources.title: Nintendo 3.0.0 fighter adjustments
sources.supports: Release-triggered perfect shield and the repeated-activation issue.

sources.supports: Five-frame release window and at least three raised-shield frames. Source supports these entry values, not the custom +11 attacker hitstop.

remaining: Parry timing, missed inputs, recovery and short-hop contacts across all fighters; multiple players, swapped sides and replay evidence. None performed by this automated pass.
Stale moves, rage and knockback formulas
Replace or verify project values against a versioned dataset; audit pre/post-hit percent, DI/SDI, hitstun, shield damage and counter rounding.
Verify parry hitstop and projectile behavior, shield drop/stun buffering, dodge fatigue, tech windows and ledge regrabs.
Add sustained analog walking, explicit action buffers, configurable tap jump and predictor alignment; independent Up does not finish these.
Resolve L-cancel, meteor-cancel, custom wavedash and crouch-cancel rules against the chosen Ultimate profile.
Define original-fighter move specifications and reference stages; the three original fighters do not map one-to-one to Nintendo fighters.
Real latency/loss, physical pads, mobile GPU memory, cold downloads, frame pacing and exhaustive action/clip reachability remain open.

damageExamples.note: Examples use the existing project freshness multiplier. One-on-one scaling is percent damage only; no additional factor is applied to shield damage or base knockback.

playtests.limits: CPU self-play is a reproducible regression sample, not human balance certification. Timeouts are not assigned winners. No fighter damage/weight buffs are inferred from these results.
